newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile tower collapse injures 44 at rock concert.
newsitem.headline: Chile tower collapse injures 44 at rock concert.

text.p: Some 44 people were injured when a sound and lighting tower collapsed in a packed stadium at the start of a concert in Chile by British rock group Deep Purple, officials said on Friday.
They had originally said 35 were hurt in the accident which happened on Thursday night at the Santa Laura stadium in Santiago after the group had played just three songs.
Two people were receiving treatment on Friday, said officials at nearby health clinics.
The accident was an inauspicious start to the Latin American tour by Deep Purple, who became famous in the 1970s with hits including "Smoke on the Water."
Dozens of people climbed up onto the metal tower to get a better view of the show, but the structure crumbled under their weight and crashed down onto spectators siting nearby.
"There were lots of people were standing up on the tower who should never have been there. It is a tremendous security problem," one concert-goer told reporters.
The accident caused chaos in the stadium with screams from poeple trapped under the tower, while dozens of spectators rushed to the emergency exits.
The organisers decided to resume the concert after the accident as they feared disturbances if it was cancelled.
